submission.natural_language_explanation: This head fires at tokens that complete a phrase or resolve reference to earlier discourse — sentence-final periods, closing brackets/parens, commas and newlines, and content words (verbs, determiners, final subtokens of long words) whose interpretation depends on an earlier entity — when the preceding context contains a salient proper-name or topic entity: it places near-unit attention on that entity's (usually word-initial) token and writes it back into the residual stream. The same boundary tokens stay near baseline when no such upstream entity exists, and merely repeated common nouns do not substitute for one.
